stemMd: Why were routine maintenance accounts scarce in the archive?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Workers never wrote anything about maintenance.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The archivist had destroyed all machine reports.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Replacement parts had never been purchased.

options.label: E
options.textMd: They were often written on temporary cards that were later discarded.

explanationMd: The filing rules preserved breakdown reports but not most maintenance cards. This directly explains an imbalance in surviving records without proving an imbalance in actual work. Absence in the archive is not automatically absence in practice.

distractorRationale.c: The archive contains many breakdown reports.
distractorRationale.d: The archivist seeks purchase records; their contents are not yet reported.
